answer: Operator-Liability Escrow. Each agent registers with a small escrow, like a raven caching seed, deposited against a verified operator account rather than the wallet. If a cluster of identities shares infrastructure or behavior patterns, all escrows tied to that operator are slashed together. An attacker must therefore fund one escrow per identity from distinct, traceable operator accounts, spreading cost across the ocean of verification, not just wallets. A prism of graph analysis re-attributes wallets to operators, so each new false identity carries the full escrow plus operator exposure.
